equivalent: belt-and-braces with the guards downstream of it. `finite` turns a bare `f64` price into the `Option` shape the other prices already have, and it has two consumers. `charge` accepts a price only under `Some(e) if e.is_finite()`, and `unpriced` reads it through `priced`, which is `matches!(x, Some(e) if e.is_finite())` — so a `finite` that passed a NaN or an infinity through hands each of them a `Some` it rejects for the same reason, naming the term unpriced and refusing the total exactly as before. `separate` sits between them and, under `Scope::AllIn`, returns `None` whatever it is given. FIXTURE (built and run 2026-09-25, a standalone crate compiling four copies of the module's non-test code side by side: unmutated, this mutant, and two controls): every output compared by `Debug` — `unpriced`, `is_complete`, `bill` (every field), `joules`, `joules_synops_only`, `understatement` — plus the bill's `Display`, for every table x ledger pair. Tables take e_syn_op and e_neuron_update from {NaN, +inf, -inf, 0, 2e-12, 5e-12}, the three optional prices from {None, Some(NaN), Some(+inf), Some(-inf), Some(0), Some(3e-12), Some(7e-12)}, both scopes and two grades (49,392 tables); ledgers take each of the six counts from {0, 3} (64 ledgers). Result: 22,127,616 comparisons, 0 disagreements. The same fixture against two non-equivalent controls, `finite` returning `None` and `finite` doubling a finite price, reports 3,578,376 and 1,239,408 disagreements, so it is able to fail.
